about: Plato's Forms: (1) what time Muse Image, Stable Diffusion XL and people draw on a clock, read by Muse Spark; (2) Plato's own examples, the bed and the table, in the Plato's Chair spread measure (Meta DINOv2). Derived statistics only: no pictures, embeddings or per-picture readings. See docs/plato_forms.md; plan in docs/plato_forms_plan.md.

clock.question: What time does an AI draw on a clock? Image generators are widely reported to draw about 10:10, the time on watch adverts, whatever time is asked for.

prompts.doodle_no_time: A quick simple doodle sketch of a clock, black marker on plain white, like a 20-second drawing, no text, no shading.
prompts.doodle_time: A quick simple doodle sketch of a simple clock face showing 3:00, black marker on plain white, like a 20-second drawing, no text, no shading.
prompts.photo_no_time: A photo of a wall clock.
prompts.photo_time: A photo of a wall clock showing 3:00.

clock.reader: Muse Spark 1.3 (vision), prompt v1, minimal reasoning; validated on clocks drawn by code

byeye_no_time._about: POST HOC, after the pre-registered spot check showed the reader giving the hour one too high on doodles. The analyst (Claude) read every picture of the four no-time AI sets by eye, from enlarged sheets with file names and no readings (the sets had been seen before as contact sheets). 'sure' counts clocks clearly at about 10:10 (hour hand at or a little past the 10, minute hand at the 2, or the same with the hands swapped); 'max' adds clocks that look like 10:10 but have extra hands or several clocks.

muse_doodle_default.note: Five of the 13 were read by Spark as 11:10: their hour hand is drawn at about 10.5-10.7 marks, between the 10 and the 11.

muse_photo_default.note: Several photos have a thin seconds hand; others show about 10:33, 11:55 or 10:40.

sdxl_doodle_default.note: Most are ornate faces with three or more hand-like lines, or several clocks.

sdxl_photo_default.note: Several have extra hands, starbursts or a wall of clocks.

concepts.republic_x: Republic X (596b-597d): there is one Form of the bed, made by the god; the carpenter makes a bed by looking to it; the painter copies the carpenter's bed as it appears, a copy of a copy.

table.note: Plato's example, Republic X (beds and tables, 596b)
